name: Golghar
description: A historic beehive-shaped granary built in 1786 by Captain John Garstin. It offers panoramic views of Patna from its 145-step spiral staircase.

name: Patna Sahib Gurudwara
description: One of the five Takhts of Sikhism, marking the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. A sacred and architecturally grand structure.

name: Mahavir Mandir
description: One of the most revered Hindu temples in Bihar dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Located near Patna Junction railway station.

name: Mahabodhi Temple
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site marking the location where Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree.

name: Vishnupad Temple
description: An ancient temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu, built along the Falgu River. Houses a footprint of Lord Vishnu on basalt rock.

name: Litchi Gardens
description: Muzaffarpur is famous as the 'Land of Litchis'. The lush litchi orchards spread across the city offer a unique agricultural tourism experience.

name: Ranchi Lake
description: A scenic artificial lake in the heart of Ranchi city, perfect for boating and surrounded by lush greenery.

name: Hundru Falls
description: A stunning 98-meter waterfall formed by the Subarnarekha River, one of the highest waterfalls in Jharkhand.

name: Canary Hill
description: A hilltop viewpoint offering stunning panoramic views of Hazaribagh town and surrounding forests. Popular at sunrise and sunset.

name: Maithon Dam
description: A massive dam on the Barakar River, surrounded by hills and dense forests. A popular picnic spot with boating facilities.

name: Golden Temple
description: Sri Harmandir Sahib, the holiest shrine of Sikhism. Its golden dome and sacred pool create a breathtaking spiritual experience.

name: Jallianwala Bagh
description: A historic garden and memorial commemorating the 1919 massacre. Bullet marks on the walls serve as a reminder of India's freedom struggle.

name: Rock Garden
description: A unique sculpture garden created by Nek Chand using industrial and urban waste. Spread over 40 acres with waterfalls and amphitheatres.

name: Sukhna Lake
description: A beautiful man-made reservoir at the foothills of the Shivalik hills. Popular for boating, jogging, and watching migratory birds.

name: Punjab Agricultural University
description: One of the largest agricultural universities in Asia, playing a key role in India's Green Revolution with beautiful campus gardens.

name: India Gate
description: A 42-meter tall war memorial arch built in 1931. A tribute to 70,000 Indian soldiers who died in World War I. Surrounded by lush gardens.

name: Red Fort
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and symbol of India's sovereignty. This magnificent Mughal fortress dates back to 1638.

name: Qutub Minar
description: A 73-meter tall UNESCO World Heritage minaret built in 1193. The tallest brick minaret in the world with intricate carvings.

name: Gateway of India
description: An iconic arch monument overlooking the Arabian Sea, built in 1924. The most photographed landmark of Mumbai.

name: Marine Drive
description: A 3.6 km long promenade along the coast known as the 'Queen's Necklace' for its glittering nighttime view.

name: Shaniwar Wada
description: An 18th-century fortification and historical landmark that was the seat of the Peshwa rulers of the Maratha Empire.

name: Aga Khan Palace
description: A historic palace built in 1892 where Mahatma Gandhi and other leaders were imprisoned. Now a shrine to Gandhi's legacy.

name: Deekshabhoomi
description: A sacred Buddhist monument where Dr. B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism. Features a massive stupa inspired by Sanchi architecture.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
description: A 240-acre botanical garden with rare plant species, a glasshouse inspired by London's Crystal Palace, and a 3,000-million-year-old rock.

name: Bangalore Palace
description: A Tudor-style palace built in 1878 inspired by England's Windsor Castle. Features Gothic architecture with fortified towers.

name: Mysore Palace
description: The official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty. A stunning Indo-Saracenic palace illuminated by 97,000 bulbs on Sundays and festivals.

name: Chamundi Hills
description: A 1,065-meter hilltop with the ancient Chamundeshwari Temple and a massive Nandi Bull statue carved from a single rock.

name: Marina Beach
description: The longest natural urban beach in India, stretching 13 km. A beloved landmark with a vibrant atmosphere at sunrise and sunset.

name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
description: A beautiful Dravidian-style temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, known for its stunning gopuram (gateway tower) and ancient history.

name: Marudhamalai Temple
description: A hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Murugan perched on the Western Ghats, offering scenic views and spiritual serenity.

name: Victoria Memorial
description: A breathtaking white marble monument built in 1921, blending British and Mughal architecture. Houses a museum of Indian history.

name: Howrah Bridge
description: An iconic cantilever bridge over the Hooghly River, one of the busiest in the world. A symbol of Kolkata's heritage.

name: Belur Math
description: The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission founded by Swami Vivekananda. Its architecture symbolizes unity of all religions.

name: Bara Imambara
description: An 18th-century Mughal monument famous for its Bhool Bhulaiya (labyrinth). One of the largest imambaras in the world.

name: Rumi Darwaza
description: An imposing 60-foot gateway built in 1784 in Awadhi architectural style. An enduring symbol of Lucknow's cultural heritage.

name: Kanpur Memorial Church
description: Also known as All Souls' Cathedral, built in 1875 in Gothic style to commemorate British soldiers of the 1857 revolt.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of the 12 Jyotirlingas dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in the spiritual capital of India. Recently renovated with a grand corridor.

name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
description: The most famous ghat on the banks of the Ganges, known for its spectacular evening Ganga Aarti ceremony.

name: Hawa Mahal
description: The iconic 'Palace of Winds' with 953 small windows designed for royal women to observe city life. A masterpiece of Rajput architecture.

name: Amber Fort
description: A majestic hill fort blending Rajput and Mughal architecture. Features the stunning Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) and scenic Maota Lake.

name: City Palace
description: A sprawling palace complex on the banks of Lake Pichola, blending Rajasthani and Mughal architecture with stunning lake views.

name: Lake Pichola
description: A beautiful artificial freshwater lake surrounded by palaces, temples, and ghats. Home to the famous Lake Palace hotel.

name: Mehrangarh Fort
description: One of the largest forts in India, perched 400 feet above the Blue City. Houses an excellent museum and offers breathtaking views.

name: Sabarmati Ashram
description: Mahatma Gandhi's home from 1917 to 1930 and the base for the Salt March. A museum showcasing Gandhi's life and philosophy.

name: Adalaj Stepwell
description: A stunning five-story stepwell built in 1498 with intricate carvings. A masterpiece of Indo-Islamic architecture.

name: Laxmi Vilas Palace
description: One of the grandest private residences in the world, four times the size of Buckingham Palace. A stunning Indo-Saracenic masterpiece.

name: Dumas Beach
description: A serene beach along the Arabian Sea known for its black sand and beautiful sunset views. A popular weekend getaway.

name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site housing the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier. A masterpiece of Baroque architecture from 1605.

name: Fort Aguada
description: A 17th-century Portuguese fort overlooking the Arabian Sea with a four-storey lighthouse offering spectacular coastal views.

name: Margao Church
description: The Church of the Holy Spirit, a magnificent 17th-century Baroque church and one of the oldest churches in Goa.

name: Fort Kochi Beach
description: A charming beach known for its iconic Chinese fishing nets, colonial architecture, and vibrant art scene along the waterfront.

name: Mattancherry Palace
description: Also known as the Dutch Palace, this 16th-century palace features stunning Kerala mural paintings depicting Hindu mythology.

name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
description: An ancient Hindu temple known for its Dravidian architecture and immense treasure vault. Dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

name: Eravikulam National Park
description: Home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr, this park features rolling tea gardens, grasslands, and the pristine beauty of the Western Ghats.

name: Tea Gardens of Munnar
description: Endless rolling hills carpeted with emerald green tea plantations. Munnar's signature landscape offering magical misty mornings.

name: The Ridge
description: A large open space in the heart of Shimla offering panoramic views of the snow-capped Himalayas and the Christ Church.

name: Mall Road Shimla
description: The main street of Shimla lined with shops, restaurants, and colonial-era buildings. The social hub of the 'Queen of Hills'.

name: Solang Valley
description: A stunning valley famous for adventure sports — skiing, paragliding, and zorbing, set against a backdrop of snow-capped peaks.

name: Rohtang Pass
description: A high mountain pass at 3,978m connecting Kullu Valley with Lahaul-Spiti. Offers breathtaking views of glaciers and peaks.

name: McLeod Ganj
description: Home of the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government-in-exile. A vibrant town blending Tibetan culture with Himalayan beauty.

name: Robber's Cave
description: A natural cave formation where a river flows through narrow gorges. Visitors can walk through the cold water inside the cave.

name: Har Ki Pauri
description: The most sacred ghat in Haridwar on the banks of the Ganges. Famous for its spectacular evening Ganga Aarti ceremony.

name: Laxman Jhula
description: A famous suspension bridge over the Ganges, said to mark the spot where Lord Laxman crossed the river on a jute rope.

name: Beatles Ashram
description: The former ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi where The Beatles stayed in 1968. Now a spiritual and artistic landmark.

name: Sanchi Stupa
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Buddhist monument built by Emperor Ashoka. One of the oldest stone structures in India.

name: Upper Lake
description: One of the oldest man-made lakes in India, giving Bhopal its 'City of Lakes' nickname. Perfect for boating and sunset views.

name: Rajwada Palace
description: A historic palace built 200 years ago by the Holkars. Blends Maratha, Mughal, and French architectural styles.

name: Charminar
description: The iconic 16th-century monument with four grand arches and minarets. The heart of Hyderabad's old city and bazaar culture.

name: Golconda Fort
description: A medieval fortress famous for its acoustic architecture, diamond mines, and sound and light show.

name: Warangal Fort
description: A 13th-century Kakatiya dynasty fort with impressive stone gateways and the famous Thousand Pillar Temple nearby.

name: Kailasagiri
description: A hilltop park offering panoramic views of the Bay of Bengal. Features a massive Shiva-Parvati statue and a ropeway ride.

name: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
description: The richest and most-visited temple in the world, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. A spiritual powerhouse atop the Tirumala Hills.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A UNESCO World Heritage 13th-century temple designed as a chariot of the Sun God with 24 intricately carved wheels.

name: Lingaraj Temple
description: The largest and most important temple in Bhubaneswar, an 11th-century masterpiece of Odia-style architecture.

name: Jagannath Temple
description: One of the four sacred Char Dhams of Hinduism. Famous for the annual Rath Yatra festival with massive wooden chariots.

name: Puri Beach
description: A beautiful golden beach on the Bay of Bengal, famous for its annual sand art festival and vibrant seafood culture.

name: Chitrakoot Falls
description: Known as the 'Niagara of India', this horseshoe-shaped waterfall on the Indravati River is the widest waterfall in India.

name: Kamakhya Temple
description: An ancient Shakti Peeth atop Nilachal Hill, one of the most powerful tantric temples in India with mystical significance.

name: Kangla Fort
description: An ancient fortification and the traditional seat of Manipur's rulers. Houses temples, museums, and the Kangla Sha dragon sculptures.

name: Living Root Bridges
description: Natural bridges grown from the roots of rubber fig trees by the Khasi people over centuries. A UNESCO World Heritage nominee.

name: Elephant Falls
description: A beautiful three-tiered waterfall in the East Khasi Hills, named after an elephant-shaped rock that once stood beside it.

name: Tsomgo Lake
description: A glacial lake at 12,310 feet surrounded by snow-capped mountains. Its color changes with the seasons — from frozen blue to emerald green.

name: Nathula Pass
description: A historic mountain pass at 14,140 feet on the Indo-China border, offering breathtaking views and a sense of being at the edge of the world.

name: Ujjayanta Palace
description: A stunning Mughal-style palace built in 1901, now serving as the Tripura State Museum surrounded by a beautiful Mughal Garden.

name: Ita Fort
description: An ancient fort dating back to the 14th-15th century built with bricks. Its name gives Itanagar (City of Bricks) its name.

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: A beautifully maintained WWII memorial honoring soldiers of the Battle of Kohima, a turning point in the Burma Campaign.

name: Durtlang Hills
description: A stunning viewpoint on the outskirts of Aizawl offering panoramic views of the entire city and surrounding valleys.

name: Karna Lake
description: A historical lake named after the legendary warrior Karna from the Mahabharata. A popular picnic and recreation spot.

name: Kingdom of Dreams
description: India's first live entertainment and leisure destination featuring Bollywood-style musicals and cultural shows in a stunning venue.
